data.body:
[P2] Preserve fractional precision for Aurora and Redshift bounds

Directed rounding preserves selection only when stored timestamps have millisecond precision. Existing Aurora/Redshift tables can retain finer timestamps from earlier Python/Java exporters; updating exporters does not rewrite those rows. For example, `since: "2026-10-23T18:42:46.784119Z"` becomes `.785Z`, incorrectly excluding a stored `.784500Z` timestamp that the previous query included. Preserve fractional precision for Aurora/Redshift bounds and restrict millisecond rounding to destinations that require it. Add a regression test covering retained microsecond timestamps.
